title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: serpent as cause of common evil — not the evil itself
pass_a_gloss: Worse for you: the same move hands Placeus weapons deadly to that charge. His chain: whatever a shared remedy fights is either the shared ill itself or what makes the ill shared. Here the remedy fights the serpent; the serpent is not itself the shared ill. So the serpent is why the ill is shared.
pass_b_english: What of this—that it even supplies me arms fatal to that imputation of yours? For I reason thus. That against which a common remedy is set is either the common evil itself or the cause why the evil is common. In this place the common remedy is set against the serpent; and the serpent is not itself the common evil. Therefore the serpent is the cause why the evil is common.
source_text: Quid quod mihi arma ministrat tuae isti imputationi funesta? Sic enim ratiocinor. Id cui remedium commune opponitur, vel est ipsum commune malum vel causa cur sit malum commune. Opponitur hoc loco remedium commune serpenti; nec est serpens ipsum commune malum. Ergo serpens est causa cur sit malum commune.
